payloads.name: stations
payloads.note: nine external stations: two wingtip, six under the wings, one centreline

loadouts.name: air superiority
loadouts.note: the article's missiles: the AIM-120 on the wingtips ('US aircraft often mount that missile on their wingtips'), the AIM-9X on the outboard stations, two more AIM-120 on the mid stations (the mix of the article's '6 x AIM-120 AMRAAM' and '6 x AIM-9 Sidewinder': assumed)

loadouts.name: mk82 x4
loadouts.note: Four Mk 82s on the mid and inboard wing stations: the F-16 carries the Mk 82 (the article's armament: 'Mark 82 GP bombs'); which stations is an engineering assumption (MS-7a's test of store management, the missiles following with their cards, MS-7b)

loadouts.name: external tanks
loadouts.note: the standard three tanks: 370 US gal on 4 and 6, 300 on the centreline (FAS: 1,040 US gal external) (ADR-30, MS-7g: a tank's fuel feeds the aircraft's own tanks; jettisoned, it flies on with what is left)

loadouts.name: pods
loadouts.note: an ALQ-184 on the centreline, as RAND's F-16C configurations carry one (ADR-30, MS-7g: a pod as a store - its mass and its drag on the aircraft; what it senses or jams is its payload's, not built with it yet)
